summary: policy alias crosswalk mismatch causing misattributed SLA coverage in weekly reports
description:
Issue summary:

We discovered that the support policy alias table (legacy_policy_aliases) contains multiple stale mappings for policy identifiers that were canonicalized during the policy-ID migration in Q4 2025. The routing-engine uses the canonical ID for live autorouting but the weekly SLA reporting pipeline joins on the legacy alias value. As a result, a subset of tickets routed by canonical ID are not being counted under the correct SLA cohort in weekly reports, producing under-reported SLA coverage for the Escalations cohort and over-reporting for a small 'miscellaneous' bucket.
impact: Operational reporting: Weekly SLA coverage for Escalations shows a 3.4% drop for last week that does not match live routing metrics or support workload expectations. No customer-facing outages observed; internal routing behaves correctly. Reporting consumers (GTM and SRE dashboards) are receiving incorrect cohort-level SLA numbers which affects prioritization and capacity planning.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Run the weekly-report join step locally against prod snapshots (dataset: support-events-2026-03-07).
2) Compare cohort counts when joining on event.policy_id vs event.policy_alias.
3) Query legacy_policy_aliases for policy aliases with multiple canonical targets: select alias, array_agg(canonical_id) from legacy_policy_aliases group by alias having count(distinct canonical_id) > 1;
4) Recreate routing decision for sample ticket id 1029384 and compare which canonical_id routing-engine selected vs which alias the reporting job joined on.
logs_and_evidence:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/SLAS/weekly-coverage?orgId=1
- Query snippets: attached BigQuery exports in /mnt/support-dumps/weekly_report_2026-03-07.csv
- Example ticket mismatch: ticket SUP-001223 routed with canonical policy 'escalation_high_v2' but reporting row shows alias 'escalation_high' mapped to legacy canonical 'escalation_high_v1'.
- Slack thread: #support (thread ts: 1678123456.000200)
initial_hypothesis: During the Q4 canonicalization some aliases were re-pointed to new canonical IDs but the alias table was never deduplicated; the indexer that materializes alias->canonical mappings for reporting kept an older snapshot. The reporting join uses the stale materialized view, whereas the routing path queries the live canonicalization service, resulting in a divergence.
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Aisha: Confirmed discrepancy between live autorouting counts and weekly report counts. Pulled sample tickets and trace IDs.
03/10 - Marco: Found 28 aliases that point to two different canonical IDs in legacy_policy_aliases; indexer last run on 2026-02-15.
03/11 - SRE (Lena Kim): Verified indexer cron failed with transient timeout on 2026-02-15 and auto-retry suppressed by backoff config; indexer service still running but uses cached snapshot.
03/11 - Analytics (Ravi): Calculated the coverage delta: when joining on canonical_id the escalation cohort had 1,842 tickets; when joining on alias it reported 1,782 tickets (3.4% delta).
temporary_workaround:
- Push a temporary mapping override: add explicit alias->canonical overrides for the 28 affected aliases in the reporting materialized view (rollbackable).
- Communicate to GTM/ops that the weekly SLA numbers for 2026-03-07 are provisional and a corrected report will be issued after backfill.
proposed_fix:
1) Patch policy-indexer to deduplicate aliases and prefer most-recent canonical mapping based on canonicalization_event_ts.
2) Add validation to the indexer: fail fast if an alias maps to >1 canonical_id and open an alert channel #support-indexer.
3) Run a backfill to reprocess historical snapshots for the last 90 days and regenerate weekly reports.
4) Deploy the patched indexer with a feature flag and run a canary against last week's data.
risk_and_rollback_plan:
- Risk: Backfill will re-materialize reporting tables and could change downstream KPIs; plan to run backfill to a shadow table first and run diff checks.
- Rollback: Keep the override in place and revert indexer changes; publish corrected report only after diff passes.
resolution: Workaround override applied 2026-03-11; indexer patch prepared and code review opened (PR 1294). Backfill scheduled for 2026-03-14 to shadow table. Final report will be issued after verification.
next_steps:
- Marco: finish PR and deploy to staging (target 2026-03-12).
- Aisha: notify GTM and SRE leads and schedule post-mortem if delta > 5% after backfill.
- Analytics: run diff checks and sign off on shadow->prod promotion.
- SRE: add alert for indexer missed runs to avoid silent cache staleness.
